name: Series
blurb: Given a string of digits, output all the contiguous substrings of length `n` in that string.
instructions:
# Instructions

Given a string of digits, output all the contiguous substrings of length `n` in that string in the order that they appear.

For example, the string "49142" has the following 3-digit series:

- "491"
- "914"
- "142"

And the following 4-digit series:

- "4914"
- "9142"

And if you ask for a 6-digit series from a 5-digit string, you deserve whatever you get.

Note that these series are only required to occupy _adjacent positions_ in the input;
the digits need not be _numerically consecutive_.
example_solution:
: slices \ s n --
  dup 0 n:> !if 2drop [] ;; then
  >r "" s:/
  ( "" a:join ) r> 1 a:map+ ;
test_code:
"series.8th" f:include
needs exercism/test
with: test
11 tests

"slices of one from one" 
    ( "1" 1 slices ) 
    ["1"] 
    equal?

SKIP-REST-OF-TESTS

"slices of one from two" 
    ( "12" 1 slices ) 
    ["1", "2"] 
    equal?

"slices of two" 
    ( "35" 2 slices ) 
    ["35"] 
    equal?

"slices of two overlap" 
    ( "9142" 2 slices ) 
    ["91", "14", "42"] 
    equal?

"slices can include duplicates" 
    ( "777777" 3 slices ) 
    ["777", "777", "777", "777"] 
    equal?

"slices of a long series" 
    ( "918493904243" 5 slices ) 
    ["91849", "18493", "84939", "49390", "93904", "39042", "90424", "04243"] 
    equal?

"slice length is too large" 
    ( "12345" 6 slices ) 
    [] 
    equal?

"slice length is way too large" 
    ( "12345" 42 slices ) 
    [] 
    equal?

"slice length cannot be zero" 
    ( "12345" 0 slices ) 
    [] 
    equal?

"slice length cannot be negative" 
    ( "123" -1 slices ) 
    [] 
    equal?

"empty series is invalid" 
    ( "" 1 slices ) 
    [] 
    equal?

end-of-tests
;with
source: A subset of the Problem 8 at Project Euler
